title: A prescription whose 'no substitution' format does not meet 105 CMR 721.020(B) is invalid and shall not be filled
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D provides that every prescription issued in the commonwealth by a practitioner shall meet the standards for format established by the Department of Public Health and that only by signing the prescription in accordance with the standards shall the practitioner validate it; it requires the standards to permit the practitioner to instruct the pharmacist to dispense a brand name drug product by indicating 'no substitution', to require that the indication of 'no substitution' not be the default indication, and to require that the prescription indicate 'Interchange is mandated unless the practitioner indicates "no substitution" in accordance with the law'. Under 105 CMR 721.003, 105 CMR 721.000 establishes the standards for format and security that all Prescriptions issued by practitioners or reduced to writing by pharmacists must meet in order to comply with M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D and M.G.L. c. 94C, and 105 CMR 721.010 defines a Prescription as an oral, written or electronic order for a medication or device which is dispensed to or for an ultimate user, not including an order for medication which is dispensed for immediate administration to the ultimate user. 105 CMR 721.020, headed Prescription Formats, provides in paragraph (A) that every Prescription generated in the Commonwealth must be an Electronic Prescription issued in accordance with 105 CMR 721.000 and include an Electronic Signature unless it is a Prescription issued in accordance with an exception listed in 105 CMR 721.070; in paragraph (B) that a Prescription must enable the practitioner to instruct the pharmacist to dispense a brand name Drug Product by indicating 'no substitution', provided that (1) the indication of 'no substitution' is not the default indication, (2) the Prescription indicates that 'Interchange is mandated unless the practitioner indicates "no substitution" in accordance with the law', and (3) the indication of 'no substitution' is a unique element in the Prescription and shall not be satisfied by use of any other element, including the signature; and in paragraph (F) that Written Prescriptions, where permitted by state and federal law, shall be issued in accordance with 105 CMR 721.000 on a form that contains the practitioner's signature, must comply with the procedures set forth in 105 CMR 721.020(B) through (F), and shall either be transmitted via facsimile or similar technology or written on a tamper-resistant form consistent with federal requirements for Medicaid. 105 CMR 721.020 does not state separately how an Oral Prescription shows the conditions in paragraph (B). 105 CMR 721.040(A) provides that a Prescription in a format that does not conform to 105 CMR 721.000 is invalid and shall not be filled. A prescription whose format makes 'no substitution' the default indication, does not carry the statement that interchange is mandated unless the practitioner indicates 'no substitution', or lets the signature or another element serve as the 'no substitution' indication therefore does not conform to 105 CMR 721.020(B) and, under 105 CMR 721.040(A), is invalid and shall not be filled, either as written or with an interchangeable drug product. A prescription in a conforming format on which the practitioner has not made the unique 'no substitution' indication is not made invalid by that omission: neither the signature nor any other element supplies the indication, and the interchange direction in M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D applies. Neither 105 CMR 721.000 nor M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D states what the pharmacist does with a prescription that is invalid under 105 CMR 721.040(A) beyond not filling it.
exam_relevance: Tests that a prescription whose format makes 'no substitution' the default, omits the statement that interchange is mandated unless the practitioner indicates 'no substitution', or lets the signature serve as the indication is invalid and shall not be filled under 105 CMR 721.040(A), rather than a prescription to be interchanged, while a conforming prescription on which the practitioner has not made the indication is filled with the interchange that M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D directs.

exceptions: A prescription in a conforming format on which the practitioner has not made the unique 'no substitution' indication is not invalid for that reason; the signature does not supply the indication, and the interchange direction in M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D applies to it.
common_confusions: Interchanging on a prescription whose 'no substitution' indication is a pre-printed or pre-selected default. That format does not conform to 105 CMR 721.020(B)(1), and under 105 CMR 721.040(A) the prescription is invalid and shall not be filled.

Dispensing the brand as written, or an interchangeable product, on a form that makes the signature the 'no substitution' indication or that omits the statement that interchange is mandated. Either defect makes the format nonconforming, and the prescription shall not be filled.
Treating a conforming prescription as invalid because the practitioner signed it without making the 'no substitution' indication. The signature validates it, and interchange is mandated.
